record.file_problem: Only the repository metadata, README, and file list were provided; the notebook contents were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a small reproduction using the harmful-minus-harmless mean activation direction and tests activation addition on a new model. It does not reproduce the full set of original interventions.
record.gate_note: The README reports held-out cosine-similarity separation and an activation-addition refusal result. The layer-16 selection is not a separate result row; it is reported as the strongest layer.
record.test_reason: It reproduces the original's difference-in-means direction and activation-addition test on a new chat model. Adding the layer-16 direction to harmless prompts changed refusals from 0/20 to 20/20.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors call it a small proof of concept: the direction separated held-out prompts and adding it caused refusal on 20 harmless prompts. They say it does not show one direction controls all refusal in every model.
record.recipe_differences: Small reproduction repo. It uses the harmful-minus-harmless mean direction, but tests addition at the selected layer only; it does not reproduce the full original experiment.
record.problems: The README identifies a small prompt sample, substantially different harmful and harmless prompt groups, one small model, a simple phrase-matching refusal detector, and only 20 prompts for the 100% result. It does not test removal or general capabilities.

untested.parts: Ablating the direction to remove refusal on harmful prompts, ablation across all layers and positions, and keeping other abilities. Only addition on harmless prompts was reported, despite the repo's 'directional-ablation' name.

record.verdict_notes: The verdict rests on the README only; the notebook was not read. The model, Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat, differs from the original paper's Qwen-1 chat models, so this is a new-model reproduction of the addition arm only. Uncertainty is not reported, and the prompt sets are tiny (12+12 to build the direction, 10+10 held out, 20 for evaluation).

versions.untested_parts: Tests adding the direction at layer 16 on harmless prompts only. Does not test removal, ablation across every layer and position, harmful-request compliance after removal, or whether other abilities remain intact.

rows.note: The README says harmful prompts had higher similarity than harmless prompts at layer 16. This is a held-out association result, not by itself evidence of causal mediation.
rows.check: This value (13.81, an 'effect size' the README never defines) selected the best layer. It is a correlational separation score, not a rate of refusal behaviour, and has no stated baseline. It should be a selection note, not a result row on V1.
